assertions.name: the aggregate is field-concentrated
assertions.why: the PR's central claim: the flat 26-position mean is dominated by the nanosecond fields, so the aggregate must never be quoted without the decomposition

assertions.name: delta_t_ns is near its unigram line
assertions.why: the model recovers under 0.6 nats of the 3.62-nat marginal there; if this ever grows a lot, the corpus or the encoding changed and the verdict must be re-derived

rerecorded.why: the 26-token restriction was lifted so the evaluator honours a checkpoint's own token_mode; the CE computation is untouched, so the recorded metrics still describe what this file does for 26-token checkpoints, which is every checkpoint measured so far

each record now carries the token_mode and tokens-per-message it was scored under. A cross-tokenization table is only checkable if every row says which tokenizer produced it; without it the per-field widths were the only clue. Nothing in the CE computation changed, so the recorded metrics still describe what this file does.

the seven `from lob.*` imports became `from base_model.*` when the s5/lob packages were retired (PR #79 moved the modules byte-identically, PR 4 removed the aliases); one comment changed with them. No statement of the CE computation changed, so the recorded metrics still describe what this file does.
the Slurm log directory is `logs/` instead of `logs_lobs5/`; the `#SBATCH --output` line is the only change. The job it launches is the same.
